agent.askRefusePublishAll: Publishing everything at once is not something this box does, and nothing has changed. A day goes on the site one at a time, after somebody has read it back — so say which day you mean, by its date or by what it is called, and the next answer shows you that day as your readers will see it, with the button underneath. If you are not sure how many are waiting, ask which days are still drafts and we will go through them one at a time.
agent.askRefuseRemove: Deleting is not something this conversation can do, and nothing has changed. A whole journal that you want gone finishes in your email, where the server sends a single-use link to a page with a button, and only that button deletes. A trip you can delete yourself, on its own page: signed in as the owner, the “Delete this trip” link sits under “Only you can see this”, and it asks once more — naming the days and photographs — before anything goes. If you meant taking a day off the site rather than destroying it, say that instead — a day can be taken down here, and nothing is lost by it.

agent.speechConsent: This sends the recording you are about to make — your voice, and nothing else — to {provider}, who turn it into text. Not your photographs, not your location history, not your contacts, not anybody's address. The recording is not kept: it is transcribed and dropped, and no copy of it is written down anywhere on this server. The words come back into the box for you to read and change, and nothing is saved until you save it. It costs one credit per {minutes} started minutes. Your voice is not used to train anybody's model. This is remembered for this journal until you withdraw it, separately from consent to send your words or your photographs.
agent.speechConsentDryRun: This sends the recording you are about to make to the built-in dry-run backend — nothing leaves this server, no third party ever hears it, and the text you get back is a canned placeholder rather than a real transcript. It costs one credit per {minutes} started minutes, same as the real thing, so testing the flow costs the same as using it. This is remembered for this journal until you withdraw it, separately from consent to send your words or your photographs.

landing.lede: Your journal is markdown and photographs in a folder you own. Write a day yourself in the studio, or hand it to an agent instead — this instance's or your own.
landing.ledeWhatsapp: No app to install, no forms to fill in. Tell your journal about the day the way you would tell a friend — a message, a voice note, the photographs you just took — and it writes the day up, with the route, the place and what it cost.

landing.pitchOwnBody: The journal is JSON and photographs in a folder you own, on your own address. One command hands the whole thing back as a zip, and you can run the same journal on your own machine. Only paper costs money.
landing.pitchOwnTitle: Your folder, and yours to take away
landing.pitchPhotobookBody: Every day is already written, dated and placed, so the book is a render rather than a project. Choose how a day should look, leave out the ones that were only driving, and the trip lays itself out.
landing.pitchPostcardsBody: Somebody asks your journal for a card. You pick one of this morning's photographs, write the back, and press send — it is printed and posted to them. The address stays with the journal; your agent never sees one.
landing.publicNone: No journals yet. Copy content/example to content/<your-name> and reload.

me.tokenBody: A key from here — or a code you read out — becomes a key that works for seven days, on this journal and nothing else. It can write days, and it can put one on the site when you ask it to; everything it writes waits as a draft until you do. It is the whole of your editing, which is why it goes to somebody you trust and never into a group chat.
me.tokenWarning: None of it is the same as being signed in here. Reading your journal in this browser cannot change it — a key can, and anyone holding one can use it. A key lasts seven days, and an agent still working can renew itself before then, so revoking is how one ends for certain.

welcome.drafts: You can see what is waiting at any time — your agent can list the drafts, and reading one back is how you check it did not invent anything. When you are happy with one, tell your agent to publish it; that is the whole of it, and nothing goes up until you say so.
welcome.draftsHeading: Nothing an agent writes is published
welcome.draftsRule: Everything written into this journal by an agent arrives as a draft and stays invisible to readers until you say it can go up. That is so you can read a day back before anyone else does — your agent publishes it when you tell it to, and not before.
welcome.footer: Sent by {site} because a journal was created for this address.

welcome.private: It is unlisted (a guest journal): it appears on no list on this server and asks search engines not to index it, so the only people who will find it are the ones you send the address to. Whether a particular trip can be read is set on the trip itself, and a new one here starts out as a guest trip too, unless you ask for something else.
welcome.public: It is public: it is listed on this server’s own index and search engines may index it. Each trip still decides for itself whether anyone can read it, and a new one here starts out public too, unless you ask for something narrower.

studio.location.what.consequence: Your phone has been quietly keeping a line of where you were. Bring it here and your trip gets a real map — the roads you took, not a straight line between two hotels.
studio.location.what.promise: This is the most private thing in your journal, and it is treated that way. The full history is never published, never shown to a visitor, and never leaves this server. What visitors see is a single line for one trip, trimmed to that trip's dates and nothing else.
studio.location.what.cta: Show me how to get it
studio.location.getIt.heading: Get the file off your phone
studio.location.getIt.intro: Google moved this onto your phone in 2024 — it is not in your Google account any more, and Takeout will not give it to you. It takes about twenty seconds on the phone itself.
studio.location.getIt.check.android: Check first: in Settings → Location → Location services → Timeline, Timeline should be on. If it was off during the trip, there is nothing to export.
studio.location.getIt.check.iphone: Check first: in Google Maps, tap your profile picture → Your Timeline. If it says Timeline is off, there is nothing from the trip to export.
studio.location.getIt.steps.android:
1 · Open your phone's Settings — not the Maps app.
2 · Location → Location services → Timeline.
3 · Tap Export Timeline data → Continue → choose a location → Save.
You get a file called Timeline.json.
studio.location.getIt.steps.iphone:
1 · Open the Google Maps app.
2 · Tap your profile picture → Settings.
3 · Tap Location & Privacy (older versions: Personal content).
4 · Tap Export Timeline data, then Save to Files in the share sheet.
You get a file called location-history.json.
studio.location.getIt.tips: Make sure you are in your phone's own Settings app, not Google Maps' in-app settings — Timeline moved out of the app entirely in 2024. If Timeline is off, there is nothing to export yet.
